slides: Let's continue with estimation, and use the numbers we know.

slides.say: Now let's use these numbers. Which number is closest to root ninety plus root twenty-six? The choices are eight, eleven, fifteen and twenty-five.
Root ninety first. Ninety is between eighty-one and a hundred, so root ninety is between nine and ten.
Now root twenty-six. Twenty-six is between twenty-five and thirty-six, so root twenty-six is between five and six.

Each root is bigger than its lower bound. So their sum is bigger than nine plus five, fourteen. Each root is also smaller than its upper bound. So the sum is smaller than ten plus six, sixteen. The sum is strictly between fourteen and sixteen.
Here it is on a number line, with the four choices. Our sum is somewhere in this band, between fourteen and sixteen.
at: Here it is on a number line

slides.say: Eight, eleven and twenty-five are far from the band, so they're out. Fifteen is right in the middle of it. So fifteen is the closest, and we never found either root exactly.
at: Fifteen is right in the middle

slides.say: And watch out for eleven. Some students add under the root, ninety plus twenty-six, and take the root of a hundred sixteen. That's between ten and eleven. But roots don't add like that, so eleven is a trap.
at: Some students add under the root

slides.say: One more example, with fractions. Which number is closest to twenty-nine over fifty-nine, plus thirty-nine over eighty-one? The choices are one tenth, a half, one, and two.
Twenty-nine over fifty-nine doesn't reduce nicely. So we look for a close fraction that does. Twenty-nine is almost thirty, and fifty-nine is almost sixty. Thirty over sixty is a half.
In the same way, thirty-nine over eighty-one is close to forty over eighty. That's also a half.
A half plus a half is one. Each fraction is a little less than a half, so the sum is a little less than one. But it's much closer to one than to a half or to two. So the answer is one.
at: A half plus a half is one

slides.say: So when do I estimate? The first sign is the choices. They're far apart in size. One is ten times another, or some are clearly too big or too small.
The second sign. The exact way is a long calculation, or I'm stuck. For example, a geometry question where I don't see the helper line, or an expression where I don't know where to start.
The third sign is in the words. When the question says about, approximately, or which number is closest to, it's asking for an estimate.
And estimates are very strong in areas and volumes, when the choices have pi or roots in them. We'll see that in the next questions.

Now the trap. An estimate works only when the choices are far apart. Look at twenty-nine times forty-one. The choices are one thousand one hundred eighty-nine, one thousand one hundred ninety-six, one thousand two hundred four, and one thousand two hundred twelve.
Thirty times forty is twelve hundred. But all four choices are close to twelve hundred, so the estimate can't choose. If I just mark the choice nearest to twelve hundred, I'll mark a wrong one.
at: Thirty times forty is twelve hundred

slides.say: When the choices are close, use another tool. Here the last digit works. Nine times one is nine, so the answer ends in nine. Only one thousand one hundred eighty-nine ends in nine.
So before you estimate, look at the choices. If they're far apart, estimate. If they're close, calculate, or check the last digit. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
